Provenance supplements

IDENTITY & CUSTODY

Signing identity

Local recorder

Loading identity…

LOCAL ENCRYPTION

Encrypt a file

Encrypt for a recipient with ML-KEM and authenticated encryption. The downloaded receipt binds the encrypted bytes to your signing identity.

Files and keys are processed locally. Keep the recipient’s decryption key to reopen the file.

Implementation and scope

This file workflow uses a single authenticated envelope and reads the selected file into memory. Large streaming archives use the separate PB-VAULT-1 implementation. JavaScript timing resistance and implementation-refinement proofs remain explicit obligations in the cryptographic evidence ledger.

SOURCE, TESTS & PROOFS

Cryptographic basis

Inspect each implementation, its normative source, measured evidence, and remaining proof obligations.

855 NIST published sample cases pass. This is sample-vector conformance, not CAVP validation or FIPS module certification.

Eight abstract Lean interface/model theorems were audited without axiom dependencies. JavaScript implementation refinement and timing resistance remain open.

Seal a ProofBundle

Build and cryptographically sign a new bundle — any registry digest × any registry signature scheme, classical or post-quantum — with Merkle root commitment. Your private key never leaves the browser.

Dual-signature seal
Seals the bundle above with two independent signatures — an ECDSA-P384 primary and an Ed25519 witness — both over one SHA3-384 digest of the canonical bundle. On verify: both valid → VERIFIED · exactly one valid → INDETERMINATE (needs investigation) · both invalid → INVALID-SIGNATURE.

Files — Universal Artifact Custody

  
Seal any file type — binaries, PDFs, models, tarballs, images. Files are read in chunks and committed under a Merkle root (RFC 6962 style, same domain separation as the bundle tree), so large artifacts hash in constant memory and any chunk can later carry a compact inclusion proof. Nothing leaves the browser.

History

  
Everything you've sealed or checked in this browser, kept in order. Each entry links to the one before it, so if anything in the history were altered, that would be detectable. You can export this history at any time as proof of what happened and when.


  


  

    
Remote sync — optional

    

      Everything above works fully offline with no configuration. Turning this on additionally
      mirrors your local ledger entries to a server you control — it never replaces local storage,
      and every seal/verify action still succeeds instantly even if the server is unreachable.

Multi-agent orchestration

  
Reads pb-lane-bus directly — the same append-only, hash-chained,
  local file transport every agent lane on this host writes to
  (~/pb/live/bus/messages.ndjson, served same-origin at
  agent/live-bus/). This is not the sealed-envelope agent mesh
  (agent/envelope.mjs, X25519 + ChaCha20-Poly1305): that protocol
  is real and implemented, but its only server is the local ProofBundle broker,
  which the operator revoked on 2026-09-23 and which this page will not
  restart. The panel below composes exact pb-lane-bus commands for
  you to run in your own shell; it does not execute them from the browser.


  

    
Encryption layers — what is actually active

    

      

        
pb-lane-bus (this panel's data)

        
SHA-256 hash chain (prev_hash), plaintext body. Tamper-evident, not confidential, not signed.

      

      

        
agent/envelope.mjs (sealed mesh)

        
Ed25519 signing + X25519-HKDF-SHA256-ChaCha20Poly1305 encryption, implemented. no server — local broker guarded (exit 81), not restarted here.

      

      

        
Bridge panel target (127.0.0.1:8791)

        
Tunneled to pb-moe-02. Serves ProofBundleBridgeEvent/v2 telemetry, unsigned at the source. Different protocol from the sealed mesh above despite sharing a port.

Full digest/MAC/KDF/signature/KEM/AEAD registry lives on the Algorithms tab — not duplicated here.

Claims Lifecycle

  
Manage verifiable claims against ProofBundles — from submission through evidence review to acceptance or rejection. Claims track the provenance of assertions made against sealed bundles.


  

    
  



  

    
Overall status
      
    

    
When several claims are made about the same bundle, the overall status is
      the weakest one — a set of claims is only as strong as its least-supported member.
      Claim strength runs from excluded (rejected) up to released (fully supported).

Live Showcase Demos

  
5 end-to-end demos. Each generates a fresh ED25519 key pair, seals a bundle with Merkle root commitment, and verifies against multiple contexts — showing all major outcome tokens with a full execution trace. All crypto runs in-browser.


  

    
Live demos — ephemeral keys

    
Each "Run Demo" generates a fresh key pair. Results are deterministic in structure (same outcome tokens per context) but non-deterministic in key material. Outcomes covered across 5 demos: VERIFIED, OUT-OF-BOUNDS, INDETERMINATE, INVALID-SIGNATURE, RESOURCE-EXHAUSTED, INVALID.
